sources.authors: Robert P. Mueller; Jonathan D. Smith; Jason M. Schuler; Andrew J. Nick; Nathan J. Gelino; Kurt W. Leucht; Ivan I. Townsend; Adam G. Dokos
sources.title: Design of an Excavation Robot: Regolith Advanced Surface Systems Operations Robot (RASSOR) 2.0
sources.reading_scope: Primary PDF text: abstract, concept of operations pp1–3, selected design/testing and lessons sections pp4–10. Not complete figure review.
sources.claims_supported: 66 kg prototype; Mars concept of 1,000 t/Earth-year, 100 m haul, 16 h mining/8 h charging, 35 trips/day.
sources.limits: Annual output is conceptual; testing is terrestrial/simulant; not lunar sustained productivity or equipment cost.

sources.authors: Philip T. Metzger; Greg W. Autry
sources.title: The Cost of Lunar Landing Pads with a Trade Study of Construction Methods
sources.reading_scope: Abstract, Table 1 pp. 5–6, Table A1 pp. 34–36, methods on grading, sintering and pavers pp. 36–44. Full economic argument and figures not reviewed.
sources.claims_supported: Explicit equipment/rate/thermal inputs and parallel-production scheduling.
sources.limits: Trade model, not construction demonstration. Thermal table 100–1120 C differs from prose 127–1200 C; reported microwave layer dimensions also inconsistent. Only table-based sensible-heat diagnostic used; no site/lunar production or pad dollar quote adopted.

sources.limits: No production-scale metal yield, sustained lunar operation or cost.

sources.title: NASA Enables Construction Technology for Moon and Mars Exploration

ancillary_review_sources: Engineering review also examined terrestrial fibre, metal deposition and DOE PV comparisons. Their prices and rates are not used as study inputs. Its DOE spreadsheet download failed with HTTP503; only published tables were read. The unavailable spreadsheet remains unexamined and is excluded from this study.
